label: Today You Will Learn
h: How to notice when prayer has become rehearsal, and a six-movement shape that lets a prayer come to rest.
body:
About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

A prayer you cannot stop because stopping feels dangerous deserves help from someone who understands both faith and obsessive symptoms. Being unable to pray at all is common in depression and grief; it is not a spiritual verdict.

label: Key Scripture
h: "Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us."

label: Meet Elizabeth
h: "I think I am praying. But it feels like worrying with my eyes closed."

label: When Prayer Has Become Rehearsal
body:
Addresses God, talks to itselfAdding "Lord" to a rehearsal does not change what it is doing.
Circles without lament or trustThe psalms do not rehearse imagined futures in ever-greater detail.
Seeks a guarantee"Promise me she will be all right." Not on offer.
Cannot come to restStopping feels dangerous.
Replaces action or helpSometimes what is needed is a phone call, or a doctor.

label: Repeating A Request Is Not Unbelief
body:
Persistent prayerKeeps asking without losing heart. Open to God's will.
LamentReturns honestly to unresolved pain.
IntercessionCarries an ongoing need day after day.
Compulsive repetitionRepeats to neutralise fear or make the prayer feel complete.

The same words can belong to any of these. What distinguishes them is what they are for.

label: A Common Belief
h: "If I still feel anxious after praying, I did not pray properly, or God did not hear me."
body: Prayer is not a performance measured by a feeling. Sometimes peace comes quickly, sometimes later, sometimes as steadiness rather than calm. It was still prayer.

label: The Tool · The Six-Movement Prayer
body:
1 · Be presentBe still before you speak.
2 · Name the realityWhat is known. The event, not the chain.
3 · Pour out your heartFear, grief, anger, desire. Untidied.
4 · Make your requestSpecific, and open to God's will. Once.
5 · Remember and discernWhat Scripture says. What is mine today.
6 · Entrust the outcomeIn words. Then rise and act.

label: Where Anxious Prayer Tends To Stay
h: Most of the prayer in pouring out and asking. Rarely reaching remembering and entrusting.
body: The answer is not to pour out less. It is to let the prayer continue.

label: Do This Now
h: Pray the six movements once, for the matter that has been turning your prayers into worry.
body:
Be present · Name the reality · Pour out · Ask once · Remember and discern · Entrust. Then do the thing from movement five before the day ends.

Pause the audio

h: Pour out your heart. Then let the prayer continue to its rest.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, I have poured out my heart.

You have heard it the first time.

I place what I cannot control in your care,
and I rise to do what is mine.

Amen.
